scope: Independently validate the completed Flash-Next native-MTP MXFP4 QAT artifact and decide whether it is production-usable in Strata.

artifact.live_hub_roundtrip: The README, LoRA safetensors, MXFP4 QAT safetensors, and held-out evaluation were downloaded again through the hf CLI; all four SHA-256 values match the publication receipt.

structure.tuned_surfaces: 18 dense/shared projections; routed experts, shared embedding, and shared LM head are frozen

independent_evaluation.comparison_to_a6000_receipt: Direction, effect size, losses, and statistical significance reproduce. Candidate top-1 is 38.3072% here versus 38.4051% on A6000 FP16, and wins are 707 versus 709; this is cross-device numerical variation, not a conflicting result.

tests.command: uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest tests/test_flashnext_mtp.py tests/test_flashnext_mtp_eval.py tests/test_flashnext_mtp_mixing.py tests/test_flashnext_mtp_train.py tests/test_export_flashnext_mtp_checkpoint.py -q

production_usability.offline_quality_verdict: validated: the exact published MXFP4 grid has a strong reproducible group-disjoint teacher-agreement improvement
blockers: No converter folds the LoRA and MXFP4 effective grid into Strata dense.bin/dense.txt or combines it with the untouched routed experts.bin.
The runtime dense path supports q8_0, bf16, and f32, not a LoRA pair or an MXFP4 tensor kind; a dequantize/repack route is possible but has not been built or measured.

The trainer optimized independent single-cell forwards with no attention KV history, while Strata's MTP drafter attends over its own KV state with a default window of 32768 cells. This context mismatch is unmeasured.
The candidate tunes self_attn.indexer.index_qk_proj, but Strata's dense MTP runtime path does not consume indexer state, so that learned component has no demonstrated serving effect.

Training used the BF16 checkpoint's shared embedding/head and experts; production binds the deployed quantized target's shared head/embedding and Q2_0 routed experts, and may restrict proposals through draft_vocab.bin. Those deltas are unmeasured.
No PyTorch-to-CUDA forward parity check, live speculative acceptance measurement, latency/throughput A/B, rollout flag, or candidate-specific rollback receipt exists.

required_promotion_gate: Fold and repack the exact effective candidate weights into a Strata rt_dir while preserving untouched experts and provenance hashes.
Prove a captured-row PyTorch/runtime forward parity check.
Measure live speculative acceptance, token throughput, and output identity/quality on representative prompts against the stock MTP and lookup fallback.
Gate rollout behind an explicit candidate flag with automatic fallback and a durable rollback receipt.

worker_evidence.parent_correction: The integration worker called draft-head substitution a blocker. That conclusion was not accepted: this candidate does not tune the shared head. The valid related blocker is train/serve precision and vocabulary-subset mismatch in the unchanged shared head.

non_claims: Teacher-logit agreement is not live speculative acceptance and not end-to-end output quality.
The 2044-pair set is group-disjoint but limited to four evaluation prompts from the same four corpora as training.
The independent MPS evaluation validates offline behavior of the exact MXFP4 grid; it does not validate Strata's CUDA graph, KV state, quantized target head, or draft-vocabulary subset.
The candidate is not promoted, not production-default, and must not replace the stock MTP runtime on this evidence.
Focused tests do not replace the full repository quality gate; that gate is run separately before publication.
No held-out retrieval test split was read.
